channel.title: Mandarin — Planet Leads Academy
channel.description: You will learn vocabulary and grammar step by step, with examples and practice. No fluency promise is made: progress depends on regular study and practice outside these lessons. Mandarin in this course is standard Mandarin as used in mainland China, written with simplified characters and pinyin, the romanisation system that shows pronunciation.

item.title: Characters, Numbers 1–10, and Counting
item.description: Lesson 2: Characters, Numbers 1–10, and Counting Chinese characters are not pictures of whole ideas in the simple sense often claimed. Many characters combine a meaning part and a sound part, and some began as pictures, but the system is a writing system with its own rules. This lesson introduces a…

item.title: Shì, Yǒu, De, and Simple Sentences
item.description: Lesson 3: Shì, Yǒu, De, and Simple Sentences Mandarin word order is generally subject, verb, object, like English, which makes basic sentences easier at first than in some other languages. The challenge is not word order but small words that do specific jobs: shì for identity, yǒu for having and…

item.title: Verbs, Time Words, and Daily Routine
item.description: Lesson 4: Verbs, Time Words, and Daily Routine Mandarin verbs do not change for tense or for person. The same verb form is used for I, you, he, she, and they, and time words or context show when something happens. That makes verb learning simpler in one way, but it means you must use time words…

item.title: Numbers to 100, Time, Days, and Places
item.description: Lesson 5: Numbers to 100, Time, Days, and Places Larger numbers in Mandarin are regular, which is good news after the measure-word work in Lesson 2. Once you know 1 to 10 and the words for ten, hundred, and thousand, you can build most numbers by combining them in order. Time and days follow…

item.title: Adjectives, Comparisons, and Describing People and Things
item.description: Lesson 6: Adjectives, Comparisons, and Describing People and Things Mandarin adjectives do not change for gender or number, and they do not need a verb to be in a sentence in the way English adjectives do. The pattern is subject plus adjective, often with hěn before the adjective, not because it…

item.title: Liking, Wanting, Ability, and Polite Requests
item.description: Lesson 7: Liking, Wanting, Ability, and Polite Requests Preference and requests in Mandarin use a small set of verbs and patterns that are easy to confuse if you translate word for word from English. This lesson separates liking a thing, wanting a thing, wanting to do something, being able to do…

item.title: Directions, Travel, and Putting It All Together
item.description: Lesson 8: Directions, Travel, and Putting It All Together Travel language brings together numbers, places, directions, and polite requests, and it is a good final test of the course because you must use several patterns in one conversation.
